messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Trouble Initializing
parts:
That's not enough context to debug. It helps us immensely
to be able to see your whole program and exactly what you
typed to R and exactly what R gets back.

When you call inits(), do you get a value? These
functions that depend on global variables can go wrong
if the globals aren't defined. It's much safer and
easier for others to read if you make your functions
self contained.

And how did you call Stan? If you provide the wrong argument,
you'll get the same problem.

I think this is largely our fault for not making our
error messages more informative --- did it find a list and
just not find that value? Did it find a list with that key that
had an NA?

- Bob

whereas it is initialized to

[1] 1 0

If you are going to initialize the parameters, you should initialize them to interior values. Ben

Daniel,

I have an older version of rstan as well and was getting your error. Changing the initialization for chi_chol_Real and chi_chol_Imag got me past it...try making them arrays as opposed to lists of matrices:

#initial values
chi_chol_Real<-array(0, dim = c(numberOfGates,chiDimensions,chiDimensions))
chi_chol_Imag<-array(0, dim = c(numberOfGates,chiDimensions,chiDimensions))
for (i in 1:numberOfGates){
  chi_chol_Real[i,,]<-t(chol(chi_Init_Real[[i]]))
  chi_chol_Imag[i,,]<-chi_chol_Real[i,,]
}

After that, you will still have the issue with pi1 and pi2 that Ben is getting.
